notes: Consumed by tools/patch-community-wasm.mjs (the offline mirror builder) and mirrored at runtime by js/unity-startup.js — the test suite checks the two agree.

The wasm-initial-heap entry is deliberately NOT a bare offset patch here: the "structural" marker tells consumers to go through parseMemoryLimits()/patchInitialMemory(), which verifies the memory section itself. prepare-build.mjs skips entries it cannot express as offset/search byte patches (entries without expect/replace), so a prepared build can never pick up the community heap value by accident.

unload-assets-always: --scan candidate func #106897 (3,136 B body, f64 constants 268435456 (256 MiB) and 4294967296 (4 GiB), 10 float compares, tail `local.get 9; end` at 52,123,560). The 11-byte pattern is unique in the pinned module (verified 2026-10-17); the bare 3-byte tail occurs 309 times and must never be patched alone. It is the strongest structural match for the IsUnloadAssetsRequired-style gate, not a proof — confirm on a device by watching the heap stay flat across room transitions, and disable with ?unloadPatch=0 (page) or --no-unload-patch (tool) if behaviour differs.

memory.name: wasm-initial-heap
memory.why: the pinned binary declares initial=32768 pages (2048 MiB) of wasm memory, backed in full at instantiation — on an iPad that alone is most of the tab's jetsam budget before any asset loads. Declaring 24576 pages (1536 MiB) instead and letting wasmMemory.grow serve real demand (declared maximum 65280 pages / 4080 MiB untouched, framework getHeapMax() agrees) turns a silent jetsam kill into either a working boot or a visible abort("OOM").

patches.name: unload-assets-always
patches.why: force the IsUnloadAssetsRequired-style gate (func #106897) to return true so room transitions run Resources.UnloadUnusedAssets()
